cards.text: Job has lost almost everything (Job 1:13-19). Elihu, a younger man who waited his turn because the others were older (Job 32:4), is STILL talking, and he's got more to say to Job. This man saved up words the way I saved up dust in that drawer: a LOT, for a LONG time.

cards.question: Elihu opens with a question for Job: "Do you think this is just?" What does Elihu say Job has been claiming?

answers.text: I am more righteous than God
I am wiser than my friends
I am stronger than my troubles

cards.text: Elihu's not done. He says Job has been asking a second question, and he quotes it right back at him. Friend, nothing stings like your own words read back to you. That's why group chats need a delete button.

cards.question: Elihu says Job asks what profit he gets and what benefit he gains apart from sin. What's the question underneath that?

answers.text: Does doing right even pay off
Why are my friends so harsh

cards.question: Elihu says he has a reply coming. It's for Job, and for Job's ___ as well.

cards.text: Then Elihu says, "Look to the heavens and see; gaze at the clouds high above you." Friend, I stood under the big sky on my first night here and felt about two inches tall. Which, to be fair, is not far off.

cards.question: Elihu has Job look up at the clouds high above him. Then he asks: if Job sins, what does he accomplish against God? What's Elihu's point?
Elihu says that if Job is righteous, God receives something He needs from Job's hand.
So who does Job's sin actually touch? Elihu says Job's wickedness affects only a ___ like himself.

cards.text: Then Elihu talks about people in trouble. Men cry out under great oppression and plead for relief from the arm of the mighty.

cards.question: Elihu says these people crying for relief also go looking for God their Maker.

cards.text: Nobody asks, 'Where is God my Maker, who gives us songs in the night.' Friend, I spent YEARS in a dark junk drawer, and the only music in there was the rubber bands I shared it with, twanging off-key.

cards.question: Elihu says God our Maker makes people wiser than the birds of the air.
Elihu says these people cry out, but God does not answer them. Why, according to Elihu?

answers.text: Because of the pride of evil men
Because of the sins of their fathers
Because of the fear in their hearts

cards.question: Elihu sums it up: God does not ___ to ___ pleas.

cards.text: Then Elihu turns it right back on Job. Job says he can't see God, that his case is before Him and he has to wait, and that God in His anger hasn't punished or taken much notice of folly.

cards.question: Job says he can't see God and his case is waiting before Him. Elihu has just said God won't listen to empty pleas. So what does Elihu say about Job's words?

answers.text: God will listen to them even less
God will answer them right away
God has already ruled for Job

cards.question: Elihu wraps up by saying Job opens his mouth in vain. What does Elihu say Job keeps multiplying?

cards.text: And that's where we set the timer for now. Trust me, friend, Job's story is FAR from done.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: "Elihu's not done." / "He says Job has been asking a second question, and he quotes it right back at him." / "Friend, nothing stings like your own words read back to you." / "That's why group chats need a delete button." It isn't the opening card, so it can have only 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the Job 35:5 quote, the line about standing under the big sky, and "Which, to be fair, is not far off." It isn't the opening card, so it can have only 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card only rewords Job 35:9 almost word for word ("Men cry out under great oppression and plead for relief from the arm of the mighty"). It has none of Papa Dorin's voice, so it reads like the verse read aloud, not like Papa Dorin telling it.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: This true or false card asks whether the line about God our Maker goes on to say He makes people wiser than the birds of the air. Card 12 has just quoted the start of that line, so the card tests a detail of how the line continues. It doesn't ask about the movement or meaning of Elihu's point. This is the same kind of detail as the bad Psalm 23 example ("What does He anoint David's head with?").

rule.text: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says. Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The card mostly rewords Job 35:14-15 nearly word for word ("his case is before Him and he has to wait, and that God in His anger hasn't punished or taken much notice of folly"). It has almost none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
